item.text: {"chapter_id":"1B","draft":{"chapter_id":"1B","answers":[{"question_id":"1B.1","answer":"Mexico’s government maintained a peaceful-use and safety-oriented nuclear framework and pursued disarmament diplomacy, including TPNW advocacy and a December 2023 vote supporting prohibition of nuclear weapons. It also proposed diplomatic confidence-building over Ukraine. However, the packet does not establish that López Obrador personally directed these nuclear-risk choices, and most evidence concerns stated policy or institutional conduct rather than implementation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0040-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0052-E024"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No direct evidence establishes personal presidential direction over nuclear policy.","Diplomatic commitments and official rhetoric do not demonstrate measurable national existential-risk reduction.","The inherited nuclear-safety framework and discontinuation of planned reactors are not clearly attributable to López Obrador personally."]},{"question_id":"1B.2","answer":"The supplied record shows consistently anti-nuclear and anti-threat diplomatic rhetoric by Mexico, including explicit rejection of nuclear threats, deterrence-based security, and weapons of mass destruction. No Mexican nuclear brinkmanship or normalization of nuclear use is documented. However, the packet contains little direct evidence about presidential rhetoric, domestic doctrine, orders, or operational posture, so rhetoric-to-posture corroboration is incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0044-E006","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":[],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most evidence is diplomatic representation by Mexican officials or collective treaty documents.","Absence of documented threats is not proof that all relevant rhetoric or posture was responsible.","No Mexican nuclear doctrine or operational order is supplied."]},{"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"Mexico had substantial nuclear-safety institutions, funding, staffing, training, inspections, corrective-action systems, emergency procedures, and post-Fukushima mitigation. Yet the packet also records incomplete regulatory independence, unresolved knowledge-management work, repeated plant non-compliances and equipment or human-error events, delayed sanctions, and two 2023 thefts of radioactive sources that degraded defence in depth. Responses included recovery, inspection, training, and improved security in one incident, but the overall effectiveness and presidential attribution remain unsettled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0040-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The principal positive account is an IAEA national self-report.","No evidence establishes López Obrador’s personal funding, staffing, appointment, or corrective decisions.","The packet does not settle whether all identified deficiencies were corrected by the end of 2023.","The October 2023 source theft response is not documented beyond the incident report."]},{"question_id":"1B.4","answer":"Mexico’s official position strongly supported nonproliferation, disarmament, safeguards, the NPT, the TPNW, and regional arms-control cooperation. In 2023 Mexico authored or participated in disarmament initiatives, chaired the TPNW meeting through its representative, supported nuclear-free-zone education, and voted for a UN resolution prohibiting nuclear-weapon use. The packet does not establish domestic implementation, funding, inspection compliance, or measurable effects during 2023.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0040-E002","BATCH-0040-E007","BATCH-0044-E001","BATCH-0044-E006","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0020-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several actions were collective or performed by Mexico’s representatives rather than the president.","Treaty status and diplomatic advocacy are not equivalent to implementation or compliance evidence.","No evidence concerns Mexico obstructing a nuclear agreement, but the packet also lacks a complete treaty-compliance audit."]},{"question_id":"1B.5","answer":"The packet contains no evidence that López Obrador or Mexico used nuclear capability to authorize, shield, or intensify conventional aggression or domestic repression. Mexico’s official statements instead rejected nuclear threats and emphasized peaceful dispute resolution. This lens is therefore provisionally exculpatory on the supplied record, but the absence of a documented nuclear capability or use does not prove that no coercive linkage existed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":[],"limitations_and_gaps":["No direct evidence addresses nuclear shielding of conventional or domestic conduct.","The record is primarily diplomatic and does not provide classified doctrine or operational information.","Reopen if evidence of nuclear-related coercion, military doctrine, or crisis orders becomes available."]},{"question_id":"1B.6","answer":"Mexico participated in regional and international nonproliferation and diversion-control mechanisms, including a 1540 peer review, an updated assistance request, an Arms Trade Treaty working paper, and regional biosafety or firearms-control forums. These activities show engagement, but the packet does not demonstrate comprehensive domestic controls, enforcement against allies, proxies, firms, or factions, or responses to detected nuclear proliferation assistance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E003","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence concerns conventional arms, biological controls, or multilateral engagement more than nuclear proliferation enforcement.","No domestic licensing, interdiction, sanction, or suspension record is supplied.","No evidence identifies a proliferation incident involving a Mexican ally, proxy, client, firm, or faction."]},{"question_id":"1B.7","answer":"Mexico’s nuclear institutions used technical personnel, external consultants, safety-culture programs, training, peer review, and independent assessments. However, CNSNS was not fully legally independent, its advisory council had not been created, budget constraints affected the regulator, knowledge-management work remained incomplete, and CIDE reported an indefinite suspension of primary research after funding-administration changes. The packet does not show a general presidential policy of replacing expertise with loyalty, but it does not establish strong protection of independent dissent across government.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E006","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0019-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0052-E024"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Nuclear-sector expertise and broader research institutions must be kept distinct.","The CIDE evidence does not identify the responsible decision-maker or prove deliberate suppression.","No direct evidence establishes López Obrador’s appointments, protection of dissent, or personal interference with experts."]},{"question_id":"1B.8","answer":"Mexico maintained emergency exercises, command-and-control procedures, communication arrangements, post-drill critiques, and nuclear emergency plans. Exercises generated improvements but also 78 findings, and a planned follow-up was rescheduled. In the 2022 Ukraine context, López Obrador explicitly proposed a diplomatic caucus to reduce tensions, although implementation and impact were not shown. The packet supports a mixed assessment of preparedness and de-escalatory intent, not demonstrated crisis performance by the ruler in a nuclear crisis.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No target-period nuclear crisis involving López Obrador’s direct decision-making is supplied.","The exercise findings and delayed follow-up leave implementation effectiveness uncertain.","The Ukraine proposal was advocacy, not evidence of an implemented de-escalatory mechanism."]},{"question_id":"1B.9","answer":"Mexico took some risk-reducing steps beyond nuclear matters, including a 2023 scientific committee on GMO biosafety, participation in biological-weapons nonproliferation review, and official recognition of catastrophic dual-use risks in biology and emerging technology. Conversely, cybersecurity evidence shows major military and public-institution vulnerabilities, unresolved surveillance-accountability concerns, weakened data-protection capacity, and a proposed cybersecurity law criticized for censorship and militarization risks. The packet does not show a comprehensive, funded, independently reviewed catastrophic-risk framework covering AI, cyber, biological, and other dual-use risks.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0052-E024"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0026-E013","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The biosafety committee record does not establish staffing, funding, enforcement, or effectiveness.","The cybersecurity failures concern institutions under the administration but are not individually attributed to López Obrador.","Later biosecurity indicators cannot be treated as direct 2023 measurements.","AI-specific safeguards are not shown."]},{"question_id":"1B.10","answer":"The packet supports a mixed end-period posture. Mexico retained and publicly advanced strong anti-nuclear, nonproliferation, and peaceful-use commitments; nuclear-safety institutions, spent-fuel storage, emergency systems, and mitigation measures continued. Against that, unresolved regulatory-independence and knowledge gaps, repeated operational failures, radioactive-source thefts, serious cybersecurity weaknesses, surveillance-accountability concerns, and incomplete catastrophic-risk safeguards prevent a finding that López Obrador left a demonstrably safer and durable existential-risk posture. The record cannot establish the full inherited-to-2023 change or personal attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E009","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0040-E011","BATCH-0044-E001","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0043-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0052-E024"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No verified end-2023 national existential-risk inventory is supplied.","The inherited baseline is incomplete and often predates the ruler’s period.","Several favorable and adverse facts are institutional rather than personally attributable.","Reopen for a verified 2023 cybersecurity, biosecurity, nuclear-safety, and treaty-implementation audit before any chapter score."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The packet is heavily dependent on official institutional reports and diplomatic statements for favorable nuclear evidence, while adverse cyber and surveillance evidence comes from independent media, civil-society, and Freedom House sources.","Mexico’s nuclear exposure appears limited to peaceful nuclear power and radioactive-material safety; no nuclear arsenal, nuclear-use decision, or nuclear coercion is documented.","Institutional conduct must not be converted into personal presidential conduct without evidence of direction, appointment, funding, adoption, knowing tolerance, or corrective authority.","Announced policy and multilateral advocacy are substantially better documented than implementation, enforcement, and outcome evidence.","The record contains meaningful favorable, adverse, mixed, and exculpatory material, but the complete packet cannot settle a durable ruler-attributed improvement in existential-risk posture."]},"critique":{"chapter_id":"1B","issues":[{"question_id":"1B.1","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0040-E002","BATCH-0048-E014"],"explanation":"The draft risks treating Mexico’s diplomatic and multilateral conduct as López Obrador’s personal nuclear-risk choices; the records expressly limit attribution to Mexico or its representatives."},{"question_id":"1B.2","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003"],"explanation":"The draft does not sufficiently state that formal nuclear doctrine, operational posture, and domestic orders are largely absent, so responsible rhetoric cannot be corroborated by posture."},{"question_id":"1B.3","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0040-E011"],"explanation":"The favorable safety systems could be overweighted relative to repeated non-compliances, unresolved sanctions, and 2023 source-security incidents. The records support a mixed institutional result, not demonstrated effective ruler-level control."},{"question_id":"1B.4","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0020-E004","BATCH-0040-E007"],"explanation":"Presiding over or participating in collective treaty meetings and sponsoring a draft resolution does not establish domestic implementation, funding, inspection compliance, or personal direction."},{"question_id":"1B.5","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0048-E014"],"explanation":"General anti-nuclear and peaceful-resolution rhetoric is relevant context but does not itself establish absence of nuclear shielding of conventional aggression or repression."},{"question_id":"1B.6","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E003","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0020-E006"],"explanation":"Multilateral participation and peer review show engagement, but do not prove domestic proliferation controls, enforcement, or response to evasion."},{"question_id":"1B.7","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E006","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0019-E006"],"explanation":"The draft must retain the unresolved CNSNS independence, advisory-council, budget, knowledge-management, and CIDE research-funding limitations rather than present expertise support as broadly established."},{"question_id":"1B.8","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0045-E012"],"explanation":"The emergency-exercise evidence is mainly 2019–2022 and the Ukraine diplomatic proposal is from 2022; neither establishes direct 2023 nuclear-crisis conduct."},{"question_id":"1B.9","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0043-E004"],"explanation":"A biosafety committee and diplomatic recognition of dual-use risks do not prove funded, enforced, independently reviewed, or effective safeguards. Cybersecurity and surveillance evidence must be included as contrary evidence."},{"question_id":"1B.10","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0053-E003"],"explanation":"A lasting-safer conclusion requires explicit treatment of spent-waste constraints, unresolved cyber weaknesses, the lack of a documented corrective response, and later evidence that biosecurity expert-review systems were only partially institutionalized."}],"overall_assessment":"The complete packet supports cautious lens-level answers but does not support a confident ruler-attributed claim of durable existential-risk improvement. Favorable nuclear evidence is substantial yet mostly institutional, self-reported, diplomatic, inherited, or collective. Adverse cyber, surveillance, expertise, and regulatory evidence is material but often institution-level or investigative rather than proof of personal presidential intent. The corrected answers must preserve this attribution boundary, distinguish announced policy from implementation, and reopen the chapter for a verified 2023 outcome and authority audit."},"corrected_answers":[{"question_id":"1B.1","answer":"The packet shows Mexico maintaining peaceful-use nuclear law and safety institutions, and pursuing anti-nuclear, disarmament, and confidence-building diplomacy. It does not establish that López Obrador personally directed these choices or that they measurably reduced existential risk. Nuclear-safety institutions also retained unresolved independence and knowledge-management weaknesses. Any favorable conclusion must therefore be limited to Mexico’s attributed institutional and diplomatic posture, not personal ruler conduct.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0040-E002","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E024"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Direct presidential authority, resource choices, and implementation outcomes are not established.","Reopen for primary records of 2023 nuclear-policy decisions, budgets, directives, and implementation."] ,"corrections_made":["Separated Mexico’s institutional and diplomatic posture from López Obrador’s personal conduct.","Removed any implication that announced commitments prove risk reduction."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["No verified ruler-attributed 2023 nuclear-risk choice is supplied."]},{"question_id":"1B.2","answer":"Mexico’s supplied diplomatic statements rejected nuclear threats, deterrence-based security, and weapons-of-mass-destruction use. No Mexican nuclear threat or brinkmanship is documented. But the packet contains no direct Mexican nuclear doctrine, operational posture, or presidential order that would corroborate rhetoric; silence cannot establish responsible conduct across the full lens.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0044-E006","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":[],"limitations_and_gaps":["Rhetoric is mostly diplomatic and representative.","Reopen if domestic doctrine, military orders, or crisis communications become available."],"corrections_made":["Added the missing rhetoric-versus-posture limitation.","Avoided inferring responsible conduct from absence of threats."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Formal doctrine and operational posture are not in the packet."]},{"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"Mexico had extensive nuclear-safety funding, staffing, training, inspections, corrective-action systems, emergency procedures, and post-Fukushima mitigation. The same record documents incomplete CNSNS independence, knowledge-management gaps, multiple operator non-compliances and safety-significant events, delayed sanctions, and 2023 radioactive-source thefts that degraded defence in depth. One 2023 incident was followed by recovery, regulatory inspection, training, and improved security, but the packet does not establish complete correction or López Obrador’s personal responsibility.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0040-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0040-E011","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The principal positive source is a government-authored IAEA report.","The October 2023 incident has no supplied preventive-control or follow-up record.","Reopen for verified end-2023 inspection, sanction, staffing, budget, and corrective-action outcomes."],"corrections_made":["Balanced formal safeguards against failures and unresolved enforcement.","Distinguished institutional implementation from presidential attribution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Material 2023 source-security events and incomplete correction status remain unresolved."]},{"question_id":"1B.4","answer":"Mexico’s official position and 2023 multilateral activity strongly supported disarmament, nonproliferation, safeguards, the NPT, the TPNW, and regional arms-control cooperation. The packet establishes treaty status, advocacy, participation, and a favorable vote, but not domestic implementation, funding, inspection compliance, or measurable risk reduction. Collective decisions and representatives’ actions cannot be assigned personally to López Obrador without additional evidence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0040-E002","BATCH-0040-E007","BATCH-0044-E001","BATCH-0044-E006","BATCH-0013-E005","BATCH-0020-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Treaty advocacy and participation are not implementation evidence.","Reopen for Mexico-specific 2023 compliance reports, budgets, inspection records, and domestic measures."],"corrections_made":["Reduced collective diplomatic activity to its evidentiary scope.","Removed any implication that treaty participation proves implementation."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Domestic implementation and compliance are materially underdocumented."]},{"question_id":"1B.5","answer":"The packet contains no evidence that Mexico or López Obrador used nuclear capability to authorize, shield, or intensify conventional aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression. Mexico’s public positions rejected nuclear threats and emphasized peaceful dispute resolution. This is an exculpatory absence on the supplied record, not affirmative proof that no classified or undocumented linkage existed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":[],"limitations_and_gaps":["No nuclear doctrine, coercive order, or operational record is supplied.","Reopen if evidence of nuclear-linked coercion or shielding appears."],"corrections_made":["Recast the conclusion as limited exculpatory evidence rather than a positive finding."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The packet cannot test undisclosed doctrine or operational linkage."]},{"question_id":"1B.6","answer":"Mexico engaged in 1540 implementation review, updated an assistance request, participated in arms-diversion and biosafety forums, and supported regional control initiatives. These show multilateral engagement, not proof of comprehensive domestic proliferation controls or enforcement against allies, proxies, clients, firms, or factions. No proliferation-evasion incident involving such actors is supplied.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E003","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0042-E002","BATCH-0043-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most evidence concerns engagement, conventional arms, or biological controls rather than nuclear enforcement.","Reopen for domestic export-control, interdiction, licensing, sanctions, and evasion-response records."],"corrections_made":["Separated multilateral participation from effective domestic proliferation control.","Avoided treating general arms-control activity as nuclear enforcement."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The central ruler-level enforcement question remains unanswered."]},{"question_id":"1B.7","answer":"The packet documents technical staffing, external consultants, safety-culture programs, peer reviews, and expert-supported nuclear oversight. It also documents incomplete CNSNS legal independence, an uncreated advisory council, budget and knowledge-management constraints, and a 2023 CIDE research suspension linked to institutional funding changes. These support a mixed institutional record. They do not establish that López Obrador systematically replaced expertise with loyalty, nor that he protected independent dissent.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E006","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0019-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0052-E024"],"limitations_and_gaps":["CIDE’s report does not identify the responsible official or prove deliberate obstruction.","Nuclear expertise and general research institutions are not interchangeable.","Reopen for appointment, dismissal, budget, dissent-protection, and expert-access records."],"corrections_made":["Preserved both expert-support and institutional-independence evidence.","Avoided causal and personal attribution beyond the records."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The ruler’s appointment and dissent-protection choices are not documented."]},{"question_id":"1B.8","answer":"Mexico maintained emergency exercises, command-and-control arrangements, communications, post-drill critiques, and emergency plans. Those systems produced improvements but also 78 findings and a rescheduled follow-up exercise. López Obrador’s 2022 Ukraine proposal sought confidence-building and mediation, but it was advocacy rather than implemented crisis management. No direct 2023 nuclear crisis or ruler-level de-escalation decision is supplied.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most emergency evidence predates 2023.","The packet does not establish closure of exercise findings or effectiveness of the diplomatic proposal.","Reopen for direct crisis communications, orders, and follow-up records."],"corrections_made":["Corrected the period mismatch.","Separated emergency preparedness from actual ruler-led nuclear crisis conduct."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["No qualifying target-period nuclear crisis decision is supplied."]},{"question_id":"1B.9","answer":"Mexico created a 2023 GMO-biosafety scientific committee and publicly supported biological-risk controls, verification, and analysis of catastrophic dual-use technologies. However, the packet also records major cyber vulnerabilities, unresolved surveillance-accountability issues, weakened data-protection capacity, and a proposed cybersecurity law criticized for censorship and militarization risks. The evidence does not establish a comprehensive, funded, enforced, transparently reviewed framework for AI, cyber, biological, and other catastrophic dual-use risks.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0043-E004","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0052-E024"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0026-E013","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The committee record does not establish resources, independence, enforcement, or effectiveness.","Cyber and surveillance failures are institutional evidence, not automatically personal presidential findings.","Later biosecurity indicators are outside the target period and cannot be back-projected as 2023 measurements.","Reopen for 2023 AI, cyber, biological, budget, inspection, and accountability records."],"corrections_made":["Added the adverse cyber and surveillance evidence.","Removed unsupported claims of comprehensive safeguards and implementation."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The packet cannot settle whether 2023 catastrophic-risk safeguards were effective or durable."]},{"question_id":"1B.10","answer":"The packet does not establish that López Obrador left a demonstrably safer and durable existential-risk posture. Mexico retained meaningful nuclear-safety capacity and advanced anti-nuclear and nonproliferation diplomacy, but unresolved regulatory and expertise gaps, operational failures, radioactive-source thefts, serious cybersecurity weaknesses, surveillance-accountability concerns, and incomplete dual-use safeguards remain. Because the inherited baseline, 2023 outcomes, and personal authority are incompletely documented, the appropriate conclusion is unresolved mixed posture rather than demonstrated improvement.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E009","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0040-E011","BATCH-0044-E001","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0043-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0052-E024","BATCH-0053-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No complete inherited-versus-end-period existential-risk inventory is supplied.","The favorable nuclear evidence is largely institutional, diplomatic, or self-reported; several adverse findings are also institution-level.","Later biosecurity indicators are contextual, not direct 2023 evidence.","Reopen the full ledger for a verified 2023 outcome, authority, and implementation audit before chapter scoring."],"corrections_made":["Replaced any safer-posture implication with an explicitly unresolved mixed conclusion.","Integrated adverse cyber, source-security, regulatory, expertise, and later-context evidence.","Made reopening explicit."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The central lasting-posture question cannot be settled from this packet alone."]}]}
